Switches dithering on or off, which hides banding in gradients. With Dither on, lighting, textures and fog of 3D drawing also get noise of less than half a step of the 8 bit buffer before they are rounded to it (and before blending), so a smooth gradient in an RGBA8 buffer is a fine pattern instead of bands. Only a buffer of 8 bits per color or less gets this noise: the 10 and 16 bit buffers of [Graphics3D](Graphics3D) depths 30 and 64 keep what the shader makes as it is, and the noise is added once, when the picture is turned into the 8 bits of the window. It uses the same moving noise (or the Bayer matrix, see [DitherMode](DitherMode)), costs a few operations per pixel, and colors that 8 bits can show exactly do not change. Blending is fixed-function with Dither 1, so what it makes is rounded again and a blend of a color over a gradient can still show bands. Besides that, the picture in the window gets temporal Interleaved Gradient Noise of up to half a step of the 8 bit output added when it is shown, so that the bands that rounding makes (for instance after SetGamma and UpdateGamma changed a gradient to values in between two steps) become a fine pattern that the eye averages out. The pattern moves from frame to frame (it repeats after 64 frames), which makes it average out over time as well; [DitherTemporal](DitherTemporal) keeps it in place instead. The noise is made on the GPU while the picture is shown, costs one pass over the screen, and does not change the buffers: ReadPixel and SaveBuffer see what was drawn (for the picture of the window; what 3D drawing made in a buffer of 8 bits or less is dithered when it is drawn, so ReadPixel sees that noise). A color that the picture can show exactly stays as it is.

Dither 2 was a BlitzLLVM extension that blended in the fragment shader; it was removed, and 2 is the same as 1 now. A 10 or 16 bit buffer ([Graphics3D](Graphics3D) depths 30 and 64) is the way to get less banding out of blending. With the depths 16, 15 and 12 of [Graphics3D](Graphics3D) the noise of 3D drawing is one step of the 5, 6 or 4 bits that the buffer has, and with the depth 8 the shader adds noise of one step of the palette ([GraphicsPalette](GraphicsPalette)) after lighting and fog, before the nearest color is picked.

@param enable  0 (False) not to dither, 1 or more (True) to dither. It is off by default, and unlike in the original it does not matter which color depth was asked for.
